questions.question: Explain why large revolts by enslaved people were rare in the United States, and name the most successful revolt in the Americas.
questions.expected_answer: Enslaved people were often outnumbered by white people; plantations were small and scattered; there were few hiding places far from settlements; white society was heavily armed with militias and patrols; punishment was death and communities were punished. The most successful revolt was the Haitian Revolution (1791-1804), which ended slavery and created an independent Black republic.

questions.question: Describe Nat Turner's revolt and explain two consequences.
questions.expected_answer: In August 1831 in Southampton County, Virginia, Nat Turner, an enslaved preacher who believed God had chosen him, led about 60-70 followers from farm to farm, killing about 55-60 white people; the revolt was crushed in about two days, Turner was captured in October and hanged in November 1831. Consequences: revenge killings of many uninvolved Black people; harsher laws on literacy, religious meetings and movement; Virginia rejected gradual emancipation in 1832; Southern fear and defence of slavery grew; abolitionists drew attention to slavery.

questions.question: Explain why the Amistad Africans were freed by the Supreme Court and why the case was important but limited.
questions.expected_answer: They had been kidnapped and transported illegally in violation of laws banning the international slave trade, so the court ruled they were free people with the right to resist unlawful enslavement; John Quincy Adams argued their case and abolitionists supported them. It was important as a victory against the slave trade and as publicity for abolition, and 35 survivors returned to Sierra Leone in 1842; but it freed no one enslaved in the United States.
